tagline: Along the young West Branch, between Canoe Place and Karthaus.
intro: The byway follows the West Branch Susquehanna through Clearfield County between Cherry Tree, near the river's headwaters, and Karthaus, some 72 miles on eleven different roads. It passes Mahaffey and the old covered bridge at McGees Mills, the sandstone of Bilger's Rocks near Grampian, Curwensville Lake behind its flood-control dam, and the county seat at Clearfield. Elk are among the wildlife along the way.

Between Lumber City and Curwensville the river runs past prominent cliffs, and below Bells Landing outcrops of the same sandstone as Bilger's Rocks show all along the valley. The Native name for the West Branch was Otsinachsin, the Place by the Rocks.

moments.title: McGees Mills Covered Bridge
moments.text: An 1873 Burr truss covered bridge spans 109 feet of the West Branch near Mahaffey.

moments.title: Cherry Tree
moments.text: Canoes could go no farther up the river here, and a big cherry tree marked the 1768 purchase line until it washed away. A 35-foot granite column took its place in 1894.

moments.title: Bilger's Rocks
moments.text: A sandstone bed over 50 feet thick has split along its joints into openings, crawlspaces, passageways and arches, with trees pushing up through the cracks.
